The last ADV I played was Hakuouki: Memories of the Shinsengumi for the 3DS. The main character goes in search of her missing father, one of the few doctors in Japan trained in Western medicine. As a potentially valuable witness, she's placed under the protective custody of the shinsengumi, the special police force of Japan's military government from 1864-1869. I picked it up because the reviews said that the supernatural elements take a backseat to the game's historical setting—it really is an interesting time period full of contradictions. You have the Industrial Revolution crashing through feudal Japan's door in the form of the warships of American imperialism. While it was true that the game's narrative focused on the period, it was generally more of a "collectible baseball card" kind of recounting that focused on particular names and dates, instead of the driving forces and conflicting interests that shaped this period and the people who lived during it. Makes me wish Warren Beatty and Trevor Griffiths were the writers instead.

Here are some sources for learning I have found helpful in my learning journey:

Youtube:

  • Nick Sibicky - Geared toward double digit kyu and some single digit kyu. Always good stuff in his lectures and games.

  • Dwyrin - Lots of Go content. Great lectures, entertaining games, and commentary on pro and amateur games.

  • Haylee - Hajin LEE - Professional player and International Go Federation General Secretary. Comments on games while she plays. Something for all levels of players here.

  • Andrew Jackson - Teaches single digit kyu classes in Seattle. Some very good content.

  • Josh Lee - Lots of great lectures. Not much new content recently, but what's there is very good.

  • Little Lamb Go - Has commented games and a few lectures. His lectures on openings are quite good.

  • Shawn Ray - Game reviews and lectures.

  • Songbirdo - A single digit kyu. Does lots of commentary on his own games. Has a series on "Get Strong at ..." books. I understand that he has worked out the copyright concerns with the author/publisher.

  • An Younggil - 8 Dan Pro! Great lectures.

Twitch

  • Twitch Go Channel - Keep an eye out here for live games. Several Youtube content creators stream on twitch.

Teachers

  • Yunguseng - In-seong Hwang's online go school. Lots of videos, live lectures, and a league with reviewed games.

  • Kaz - Kaz is a former Go insei and Tokyo regional Igo representative. Great teacher.

Books

I don't have a lot of books, but here are a few I find helpful. I'm sure other people have more suggestions.

  • Essential Life and Death Series
  • Get Strong at Invading
  • Get Strong at Attacking
  • Whole Board Thinking in Joseki
  • The Workshop Lectures - Yilun Yang

There are so many more, but this is a good starting point.
